text:
lin (arch): Putting this here: Compat Conductor proposal. Instead of a single harmonizer binary, run a small orchestration layer that picks translation strategy per-route (lightweight map, deep normalizer, passthrough) and records provenance. Helps us tune per-customer policies.

omar (eng-platform): Nice. Per-route decisions would let us limit translations that blow up token counts. How do you envision policy lookup? header? tenant config?

lin (arch): Tenant config + route metadata. Priority: tenant flag override, route whitelist, global fallback. Expose via admin API and feature flags.

mai (eng-runtime): Implementation modes: 1) inproc library with strategy registry, 2) sidecar that calls out to conductor service, 3) edge gateway decision in front of all runtime clusters. We should benchmark memory/latency/cost for each.

lucy (eng-infra): Operationally, a stateful conductor service is more to run, but gives us richer rollout semantics (canary by tenant, slow ramp). Sidecar duplicates runtime memory but keeps conductor thin.

lin (arch): Key non-functional reqs: observable translation lineage (which strategy used, rule id), deterministic mapping, and a compact error model that maps to client-visible codes so SDKs can surface a deprecation warning.

sasha (eng-ml): From a semantics POV we need a strategy registry with model-aware transforms. For example, v1->vNext mapping for chat vs. completion should be distinct. Also tag transforms with expected token_multiplier so we can estimate cost.

mai (eng-runtime): Good call. We'll need the conductor to annotate cache keys: e.g., include "translated:true;strategy=slotfill;rule=R-123" so runtime knows whether to use a separate KV cache or reuse existing. Otherwise token inflation will poison caches.

lin (arch): Example header/annotation sketch: X-Compat-Strategy: slotfill;X-Compat-Rule: R-123;X-Orig-Version: v1;X-Translation-Id: uuid

mai (eng-runtime): Also we should attach X-Compat-TokenRatio: 1.35 so billing/observability can account for expected tokens.

omar (eng-platform): UX: SDKs should emit a soft deprecation warning when they detect server-side translation (200 with X-Compat-Translated: yes) so integrators start moving. But we must avoid spammy logs. Suggest rate-limit warning per-client-key.

lin (arch): Rollout idea: start by offering "diagnostic-only" mode where conductor runs but returns translations in response header without applying; customers opt-into actual rewrites later. We can collect conversion success and quality signals before touching production traffic.

sasha (eng-ml): We'll make a diagnostic harness: send stored customer prompts through translation flow and compare model outputs with native vNext outputs. We'll compute BLEU-like and a custom instruction-preservation score. If scores diverge > threshold we block that rule.

lucy (eng-infra): Security: translated payloads must preserve client-sent signatures where present. If a tenant signs requests, conductor must either re-sign (with tenant-managed key) or return a translated payload with provenance but not modify signature. Pls list KMS options.

lin (arch): Good catch. Option matrix: A) don't touch signed requests (passthrough), B) re-sign with tenant delegated key, C) require tenant to allow translation by opt-in and ephemeral signing. We'll document.

mai (eng-runtime): Failure modes: silent quality regression, token overage for customers, cache divergence. For each we need alerting and automated rollback. Suggest: quality alert + immediate disable of translation for affected tenant and create incident.

omar (eng-platform): Metrics to surface to customers: translation_hits, estimated_extra_tokens, rule_blocked_count, diagnostic_match_rate. Also expose logs with X-Translation-Id for troubleshooting.

lin (arch): Config model: rules = [ {id, matcher, strategy, priority, token_estimate, owner, block_on_quality_fail:true/false} ] matcher can be path regex + header predicates + tenant attributes.

sasha (eng-ml): We'll start by building rule pack for two canonical cases: 1) legacy-completion -> messages, 2) instructions->structured messages. Each rule will include test vectors and expected equivalence criteria.

lucy (eng-infra): Cost baseline: conductor-service ~2x pods (replicated), adds ~40ms median if external. Sidecar adds ~250MB per runtime pod. Inproc adds ~0.7ms median but couples deploys. Need to present cost vs latency tradeoff to PM.

mai (eng-runtime): Suggest POC approach: implement conductor as a lightweight library with pluggable remote decision API. Default to local lib that can call a remote conductor for policy. That gives us fallthrough to remote mode without bloating runtime early.

omar (eng-platform): Can we leverage existing feature flag infra for per-tenant policy toggles? Should be straightforward to reuse.

lin (arch): Yes, integrate feature flags for rollout. Also add a kill-switch endpoint to turn off all translations globally.

mai (eng-runtime): Sample mapping (simplified):
```json
// legacy request
{ "instructions": "Translate to Yoda speak", "max_tokens": 200 }
// conductor output -> canonical
{ "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Translate to Yoda speak"}], "meta":{"orig":"legacy", "rule":"R-legacy-01"} }
```

lin (arch): Timeline proposal: 1) spec + rule pack (2 weeks) 2) local-lib POC + unit tests (2 weeks) 3) diagnostic run + ML eval (2 weeks) 4) canary (1%) + metrics (2 weeks) 5) ramp. Total ~9 weeks to broad opt-in.

sasha (eng-ml): I'll prioritize the evals for those two rule packs. Need access to historical prompts — @omar can you help export a small sanitized corpus?

omar (eng-platform): Yep, will provision a sanitized sample set and feature-flag hooks.

lucy (eng-infra): I'll run cost/latency sims for the three modes and add numbers to the proposal doc.

mai (eng-runtime): I'll draft a minimal lib interface: translate(request, ctx) -> (translated_request, annotations, metrics). Keep it sync/async neutral.

lin (arch): Decision for this thread: approve POC for "Conductor-as-lib with remote policy option" and build rule pack for two initial transformations. Owners: mai (lib), sasha (evals), lucy (infra sims), omar (data + flags). Reconvene in 1 week.

devops-bot: POC ticket created: INFRA-8943. Conductor POC milestone due 1719028000.

omar (eng-platform): tagging owners @mai @sasha @lucy 44D

lin (arch): cool. We'll capture runbook (kill-switch, per-tenant disable, incident playbook) in the RFC follow-up doc. Thanks everyone.
